  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Path**                                          **Purpose / required update**
  ------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------
  knowledge/00-System/PROJECT_INDEX.md              Authoritative pointers to approved baselines, active
                                                    release/module and operational files. MUST record
                                                    the exact governing artifact identity and
                                                    cryptographic content hash (SHA-256 or equivalent)
                                                    for VEYRO-MPB-1.0, Veyro TSD v1.4.1,
                                                    VEYRO-UX-V1-170-APPROVED, and the currently promoted
                                                    governing EIP. The governing EIP entry MUST identify
                                                    VEYRO-EIP-1.4.1-20260827 and bind the exact content
                                                    hash of this promoted artifact; any missing,
                                                    ambiguous or mismatched identity/hash stops
                                                    implementation until reconciled.

  knowledge/00-System/CURRENT_STATE.md              Current module/gate, branch/commit, environment,
                                                    completed/next action, blockers, open defects and
                                                    evidence summary.

  knowledge/00-System/SESSION_BOOTSTRAP.md          Deterministic startup read order and checks. MUST
                                                    verify every governing baseline artifact
                                                    ID/versioned identity and content hash recorded in
                                                    PROJECT_INDEX.md against the artifact actually in
                                                    use; any mismatch, missing hash or ambiguous
                                                    identity stops implementation until reconciled and
                                                    the durable index is corrected.

  knowledge/00-System/DEVELOPMENT_CONSTITUTION.md   Copy/reference of non-negotiable execution rules.

  knowledge/00-System/CURRENT_HANDOFF.md            Exact next-session handoff; replaced each session.

  knowledge/03-Modules/MOD-xxx/STATUS.md            Module lifecycle state, dependencies, gate checklist
                                                    and approval status. For every prerequisite edge
                                                    record dependency state, SOFTWARE_ONLY
                                                    boolean/justification, gated-capability non-use
                                                    evidence and proof reference.

  \.../REQUIREMENTS.md                              Mapped requirement/screen/TSD contract scope.

  \.../SCENARIOS.md                                 Reviewed Scenario Catalog; stable IDs and
                                                    traceability.

  \.../TEST_RESULTS.md                              Deterministic automated/integration/E2E results and
                                                    run references.

                                                    classifications.

                                                    record/evidence.

                                                    state.

                                                    secrets/restricted data.

                                                    indexes.

  knowledge/00-System/EXTERNAL_GATES.md             Durable mirror of §22.0: EXT IDs, gate class(es),
                                                    explicit Gated capability, owner, blocking
                                                    modules/actions/waves, evidence, status and last
                                                    verification. Read every session; Notion is
                                                    re-synchronized from this file when divergent. For

                                                    SOFTWARE_ONLY decision and gated-capability non-use
                                                    proof; QUALIFICATION does not permit consumption of

# Appendix F. Canonical Screen-to-Module Mapping

# Surface vocabulary mapping for the 170-screen V1 count model: Admin Web maps to Admin (85); Front Desk, POS, Kiosk and Staff Kiosk map to Front Desk & POS (16); Coach App maps to Coach (19); Member App and any V1 Member Web screen map to Member (35); Internal SaaS Console maps to Internal SaaS Console (15). Developer Portal, Corporate Portal, Tenant Billing Portal, Learning Portal, Partner Portal and Franchise Portal are post-V1 surfaces unless an exact approved V1 Screen ID exists in the canonical registry; they must not invent V1 IDs and default to "no V1 Screen IDs expected".

The approved V1 design registry is the only authority for exact Screen
IDs. This plan does not invent or renumber them. MOD-001 must import the
canonical registry and materialize contracts/ui/screen-contracts.yaml
plus the generated mapping rows below before any UI-bearing module can
become Ready. The release gate is exact: Admin 85 + Front Desk & POS
16 + Coach 19 + Member 35 + Internal SaaS Console 15 = 170; canonical V1
registry count = manifest count = frontend route-registry V1 count =
170. Any mismatch is blocking. The canonical source artifact must be
checked into or deterministically referenced by the Veyro repository
before MOD-001 approval; screenshots, remembered names, inferred routes
or newly invented identifiers are not acceptable substitutes.

- Generated row schema: screen_id → surface → route → owning
  implementation module → wave → owner_domain → primary read model/query
  → commands → permissions → realtime → masking/offline/error-state
  contract. Mapping is generated from source metadata and module/domain
  ownership; hand-authored placeholder Screen IDs are forbidden.

# Appendix G. Per-Module Required Scenario Category Matrix

R = Required when applicable and must be manually executed by Claude for
the current module before approval. N = not applicable and requires a
per-module justification in G.4. O is permitted only for ALT, LOC and
A11Y when those categories are not promoted by §9.1; a §9.1-listed
category may never be O. Every non-R cell for a §9.1-listed category
requires a written G.4 applicability justification. Critical
requirements and
money/access/identity/consent/restricted-data/tenant-isolation/safety
scenarios can never be downgraded.

## G.4 Per-Module N/A Justification & Consistency Gate

Appendix G is generated from each module's objective, manual-QA
obligation, security scope, load/performance scope, integration/offline
characteristics and canonical screen ownership --- never from risk class
alone. CI/board consistency is blocking: Security scope beginning
"Mandatory" may not coexist with SEC=N; non-N/A Load/performance may not
coexist with PERF=N; Load/performance=N/A may not coexist with PERF=R;
every non-R cell for a §9.1-listed category requires a per-module G.4
justification; a §9.1-listed category may never be O; and any module
whose objective/card names idempotency, recovery, concurrency, privacy
or provider integration may not mark the corresponding category N. The
"no canonical screen" justification may not be used by any module that
owns/qualifies localization, RTL, accessibility or shared UI
infrastructure, or whose manual-QA field names Arabic/RTL, VoiceOver,
TalkBack, dynamic type or keyboard navigation.

# Appendix H. Automated Skills, Rules & Engineering Capability Governance

This appendix is normative for capability automation. It defines how
Claude automatically selects, discovers, creates, installs, reviews,
qualifies, registers and reuses engineering capabilities without
requiring the owner to manually choose routine Skills or Rules. It does
not authorize spend, trusted-source bypass, production actions or
architecture changes.

## H.1 Machine-Readable Capability Manifest

MOD-000 defines contracts/engineering/module-capabilities.yaml. Before
Scenario Review can PASS, the active module has a manifest row
containing: module_id; applicable capability profiles; repository
paths/surfaces; required agent roles; required Rule IDs; required
Skill/tool IDs; required cross-cutting controls; missing-capability
blockers; CAP/SKL/RULE evidence IDs; and status. The manifest is derived
from approved scope and is not a free-form developer preference. The
manifest must also record capability dependency IDs, per-gap
resolution-attempt counters/budget evidence, lifecycle review state and
rollback target where applicable. MOD-029 is a mandatory
privileged-surface binding: its manifest row MUST include
admin/privileged-console and the privileged-console-review check;
omission blocks the Capability / Rules / Skills gate.

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  -------------- ------------------ ---------------------------- ----------------------------
  CAP-\<NNN\>    Capability         type, source,                Required for every new
                 decision /         version/ref/hash,            external or custom
                 registry item      profile/module, permissions, capability; re-evaluate on
                                    data/network access, risk,   material change or review
                                    owner/reviewer, operational  due date. Overdue,
                                    status, lifecycle status     DEPRECATED or REVOKED
                                    ACTIVE/DEPRECATED/REVOKED,   capability cannot satisfy a
                                    last reviewed at, next       module capability gate.
                                    review due, rollback         
                                    target/procedure             

  SKL-\<NNN\>    Project/external   skill path/name,             Independent review + eval
                 Skill record       description, invocation      before ACTIVE;
                                    policy, source, supporting   project-scoped by default;
                                    files/scripts, allowed       dependencies must be

## H.2 Default Project Capability Layout

## Rule-family definition: a rule family is one top-level .claude/rules/\<family\>/ directory. The 11 governed families are global, backend, admin, web, frontdesk-pos, mobile, ios, android, edge, data-ai and infra. Every H.2 family must resolve to at least one H.3 content standard; one H.3 standard may resolve multiple families only when it names those families explicitly.

## H.3 Rule Content Standards

- Global rules encode only durable Veyro-wide constraints: precedence,
  tenant context, domain ownership, evidence, security, test/QA and
  owner/external boundaries. This standard resolves the global rule
  family declared in H.2.

- Backend rules enforce the approved modular-monolith/FastAPI
  architecture, explicit application/domain boundaries,
  transaction/idempotency/reconciliation rules, PostgreSQL
  constraints/RLS, migration safety, observability and load impact
  without forcing unnecessary abstractions. This standard resolves the
  backend rule family declared in H.2.

- Admin/Web rules (this standard resolves both the admin and web rule
  families declared in H.2) enforce Design System/component reuse,
  reusable UI primitives, typed API boundaries, permission-aware UX,
  state handling, accessibility and Arabic/RTL. New components are
  created only when an existing approved component cannot satisfy the
  requirement cleanly. The named admin/privileged-console rule family
  applies to Internal SaaS Console privileged flows and must encode
  impersonation reason/approval, explicit start/end, support-access time
  limits, visible banner, break-glass/elevated-permission boundaries,
  tenant-switch safeguards, privileged-action auditability and
  diagnostics-data minimization/redaction.

- Front Desk/POS rules enforce touch+keyboard usability, fast member
  lookup, explicit financial/access consequence states, local-device
  bridge boundaries, bounded degraded/offline behavior, explicit
  retry/recovery and reconciliation, and prohibit hidden payment or
  access mutations. This standard resolves the frontdesk-pos rule family
  declared in H.2.

- Mobile rules enforce KMP/Compose shared-by-default architecture,
  strict commonMain/platform boundaries, reusable Design System
  components, immutable presentation state, bounded offline
  synchronization, accessibility/RTL and documented native escape
  hatches. This standard resolves the mobile rule family declared in
  H.2. Mobile rules also require encrypted Restricted local caches with
  platform-wrapped per-install keys, explicit TTL/purge behavior,
  capture protection for Restricted content, and no secret/key material
  in common Compose state or backups.

- iOS platform rules enforce a minimal iOS host and strict
  native-capability boundaries for Keychain/Secure Enclave, Face
  ID/Touch ID, APNs/background tasks, Wallet/Apple Pay, HealthKit,
  camera/NFC and platform policy; SwiftUI/UIKit interop is used only
  where the approved native escape hatch requires it, without forking
  shared domain/data logic. This standard resolves the ios rule family
  declared in H.2. iOS rules additionally require
  NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication or stronger, App
  Attest on rotating-credential/abuse-sensitive endpoints, capture
  protection for Restricted screens, and TLS public-key pinning with
  backup pin plus signed rollover.

- Android platform rules enforce a minimal Android host and strict
  native-capability boundaries for Keystore/biometrics, FCM/background
  work, Health Connect, NFC/camera and platform permissions; native
  Compose/platform-specific UI is used only when justified by the
  approved native escape hatch, without forking shared domain/data
  logic. This standard resolves the android rule family declared in H.2.
  Android rules additionally require restricted-data backup exclusion,
  Play Integrity on rotating-credential/abuse-sensitive endpoints,
  capture protection for Restricted screens, and TLS public-key pinning
  with backup pin plus signed rollover.

- Edge rules enforce bounded offline authorization, signed/mTLS device
  trust, safe clock/snapshot policies,
  replay/idempotency/reconciliation, diagnostics and life-safety fail
  behavior. This standard resolves the edge rule family declared in H.2.

- Data/AI rules enforce tenant-safe lineage and semantic metric
  ownership, restricted-data policy, model-gateway and retrieval
  authorization boundaries, guarded tools, evaluation and
  prompt-injection defenses, and human approval for high-risk actions;
  AI capabilities never gain direct database authority or bypass
  tenant/security policy. This standard resolves the data-ai rule family
  declared in H.2.

- Infra/SRE rules enforce reviewable infrastructure-as-code, least
  privilege, externalized secrets, reproducible environments,
  rollback/canary controls, cost tags/budgets, OpenTelemetry/SLO/DR
  evidence and release readiness; no Production action or paid capacity
  commitment may execute without the approvals required by DC-16. This
  standard resolves the infra rule family declared in H.2.

- Rules are not allowed to encode vague slogans such as "always use
  Clean Architecture." They must state concrete, testable constraints
  appropriate to Veyro and avoid overengineering.

## H.5 Capability Qualification and Regression

- Every new Skill/Rule must have at least one success-path eval and one
  failure/negative eval; security-sensitive capabilities also require
  abuse/prompt-injection/permission-negative tests.

- A Skill that executes commands or uses MCP/network access must prove
  least privilege and demonstrate that unapproved destinations/data are
  not accessed.

- A Rule change must be tested against representative matching and
  non-matching paths so path scoping is correct and does not pollute
  unrelated contexts.

- Critical capability failures create BUG/CAP evidence and block the
  active module. Fix → independent re-review → re-eval → affected
  regression follows the same evidence discipline as product code.

- Periodic capability review is mandatory in addition to trigger-based
  re-evaluation. Every CAP/SKL/RULE record carries last reviewed at,
  next review due and lifecycle status ACTIVE/DEPRECATED/REVOKED. Once
  next review due is exceeded, the capability is immediately ineligible
  to satisfy the Capability / Rules / Skills gate until an independent
  re-evaluation passes and the dates/status are refreshed. DEPRECATED
  and REVOKED capabilities cannot be activated for new module work.

- Capability-resolution and dependency safety are bounded controls. A
  capability gap permits at most two external candidate evaluations and
  one custom project Skill/Rule creation attempt within the CAP-recorded
  45-minute default orchestration budget and, when observable,
  50,000-token budget. Exhaustion becomes BLOCKED: CAPABILITY_GAP.
  Capability/Skill dependency graphs must be acyclic; cycle detection is
  a blocking qualification and MOD-001 validation check.

- Capability versions are pinned or otherwise reproducibly identified
  where practical. Auto-updates that change
  code/instructions/permissions require re-evaluation before the
  capability can support a module approval gate.

## H.6 Owner Experience

Normal owner interaction remains goal-level: continue Veyro development
under the approved Engineering Implementation Plan. The orchestrator
chooses models, agents, Rules and Skills automatically. Owner
intervention is requested only for DC-16 reserved actions, explicit
external certification/real-world gates, organization/account
restrictions that make a required assurance tier impossible, or a
genuinely high-risk capability action that policy marks owner-reserved.
